clue.text: Following end of address, enchanted girl returns swiftly

indicators.note: following tells us one piece comes after another in the build-up

blocks.note: .org is a common ending of a web address
Ella Enchanted is the children's novel and film about a girl under a spell

explanation.surface: A spellbound girl rushes home after the end of a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: ORG + ELLA, then the whole thing reversed, gives ALLEGRO. 'Address' suggests a speech or a postal address, but it is a web address.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical direction meaning play at a brisk, lively tempo.

indicators.note: heard means we go by how the words sound when spoken rather than their spelling

blocks.note: Paul is another Guardian setter, so a setter's can be a Paul's

explanation.walkthrough: Paul is one of Yank's fellow Guardian setters; 'a Paul's' said quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to shock and dismay them, the same as horrify.

explanation.definitionFit: Lesage wrote comedies for the Paris stage, so he is a playwright.

blocks.note: great means large
gross can mean very fat or bulky

explanation.surface: A large, chunky block or die.
explanation.walkthrough: A gross is twelve dozen (144); a great gross is twelve gross, 1,728, which is twelve cubed.
explanation.definitionFit: A great gross equals 12 × 12 × 12, so the number is a perfect cube.

clue.text: Old enough for cigarette, in Old England

indicators.note: in places one item inside the letters of another

blocks.note: OE is short for Old English, a stock crossword abbreviation
fag is British slang for a cigarette

explanation.surface: Being old enough to buy cigarettes in England of old.
explanation.walkthrough: Fag is everyday British slang for a cigarette; 'Old' appears twice, once opening the definition and once in the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of age has reached the legal age for some activity, so is old enough.

indicators.note: music transposed is shifted around, so the letters are moved into a new order
the intro is the opening, so the first letter is let fall

blocks.note: ariettas are short arias, taken as written

explanation.surface: A brilliant musician has transposed some little songs and cut their introductions.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first A of ARIETTAS, then rearrange RIETTAS. The musical surface makes 'transposed' look like a key change.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a skilled professional performer, a virtuoso of the stage.

indicators.note: said means the words are taken as spoken, not as spelled

blocks.note: an arc is a curving turn
the political right is conservative

explanation.walkthrough: An ark is an old word for a chest or coffer, and a wright is a maker, so an arkwright made chests.
explanation.definitionFit: An arkwright was a craftsman who built chests and coffers, a kind of cabinetmaker.

indicators.note: in reverse means going backwards, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: a trot is a slow run

explanation.surface: Running a car backwards, perhaps on account of the battery.
explanation.walkthrough: In law, battery (unlawful physical contact) is one example of a tort; 'perhaps' flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A tort is a civil wrong, and battery is a classic instance of one.

clue.text: Animated videos about American method of cooking

indicators.note: animated means set in lively motion, so the letters move around
about means surrounding, so one set of letters wraps round another

blocks.note: taken as written
US is the usual abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Cartoon videos about an American way of preparing food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps the rearranged letters round the abbreviation, splitting them after the second letter. Sous-vide is French for 'under vacuum'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sous-vide is a technique of cooking vacuum-sealed food slowly in a water bath.

definitions.note: the clue's possessive 's is read as 'is'

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Shoppers are disgusted by impolite service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like 'disgusting', but it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: End users are the people who finally use a product, its consumers.

clue.text: Old Yank's escaping from blind alley

blocks.note: Yank is the setter, so Yank's (Yank is) is I'M from the setter's point of view

explanation.walkthrough: Yank is this puzzle's setter, so 'Yank's' stands for I'M; remove it from IMPASSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Passé means out of date or no longer fashionable, so old.

blocks.note: surface reading: canvass people's views on a style of Jamaican music

explanation.surface: Polling people about what they think of ska music.
explanation.walkthrough: SKA with its first letter carried round to the end becomes ASK, so the second word is a playful instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask around is to consult a number of people for their views.

clue.text: Kinky hairstyle takes Go-Gos' leader far

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer's wild hairdo carries the band's frontwoman a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: HAIRSTYLE plus G, rearranged. 'Far' is used adverbially here, as in 'light years better'.
explanation.definitionFit: Light years, used figuratively, means a very great distance or degree, hence far.

explanation.definitionFit: Ives co-ran a famous print business making lithographs, so he was a lithographer.

blocks.note: first meaning: the person in charge of the show in the big top

explanation.walkthrough: Quasimodo rang the bells of Notre-Dame, so he was a master of ringing; the question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringmaster presents the acts in a circus ring, the central figure of the show.

clue.text: Street performer who produces liver pâté?

blocks.note: first meaning: a busker who cranks a barrel organ
second meaning, read literally: one who grinds up an internal body part to make a paste

explanation.walkthrough: The liver is an organ, and pâté is made by grinding it, so the busker's title can be read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ grinder plays a hand-cranked barrel organ in the street for coins.

blocks.note: Jane Eyre is the governess heroine of Charlotte Brontë's novel
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Jane Eyre is the famous fictional governess; her surname is pronounced like the answer's first word. 'Crack' looks like an adjective (expert) for the pilots.
explanation.definitionFit: An air pistol is a handgun firing pellets by compressed air, a kind of weapon.

indicators.note: cried means called out, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: gall is cheek or nerve, as in 'the gall of it!'

explanation.surface: A one-time head of state exclaimed at someone's cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: Exclaiming 'the gall!', perhaps in a French accent, gives the surname of Charles de Gaulle, president of France 1959–69.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles de Gaulle served as President of the French Republic in the 1960s.

blocks.note: a fig is a thing of no value, as in 'not worth a fig'
wee is informal for urine

explanation.surface: A tiny carved ornament that is worth nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' poses as Scots for small, which suits a carving, but it is the bodily fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurine is a small sculpted statuette, which may be a carving.

clue.text: Sexy great tit flying way out

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An attractive songbird flies off on its way out.
explanation.walkthrough: The great tit is a common European songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit strategy is a planned means of leaving a situation, a way out.

blocks.note: Noah's ark is the ship
a pair is a group, and fitting for the ark since the animals went in two by two

explanation.surface: A crew working hard on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The animals boarded Noah's ark two by two, which is why the setter adds 'appropriately'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at work is occupied with their job, so busy.

blocks.note: a brand is a trade name
y is an algebraic unknown

clue.text: Sit alongside big brass that's left-leaning

blocks.note: the tuba is the largest brass instrument

explanation.walkthrough: 'Big brass' suggests senior officials and 'left-leaning' their politics, but it is a musical instrument written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to lie next to and touch, so sit alongside.

clue.text: Expert on ports, 90, stripped in embrace of profligate spender

blocks.note: the number written out
a waster squanders money

explanation.surface: A dock inspector in his nineties, undressed and hugged by a spendthrift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ports' looks like harbours, but here it means the fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine taster judges wines professionally, and port is a fortified wine.

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: I cry aloud, then check out

explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to look them over closely, which is to check them out.

clue.text: Screw that will be ready for use

explanation.walkthrough: Screw is British slang for a prison officer; the surface suggests a fixing screw tightened ready to use.
